# Eight Portable Mars Harness Skills

Purpose: define platform-neutral work-product contracts that turn model intelligence into governed mission capability.

These are capability blueprints, not personified agents and not installed software packages. They can be implemented in Codex, Claude Cowork, Hermes, Gemini, Grok or another controlled runtime. Portability requires the same inputs, outputs, evidence controls and approval gates; it does not imply identical model behavior.

## Common control envelope

Every skill must:

- Assign each claim one epistemic status: Observed, Derived, Assumed or Unknown.
- Record provenance separately.
- Preserve dissent, failed tests and negative findings.
- Identify the accountable owner and required approval.
- Produce a durable, versioned work product.
- Stop at the gate when required evidence is missing.

## 1. Evidence Grounding

Purpose: turn a mission question into a bounded, traceable evidence base.

- Inputs: question, decision context, scope, trusted-source policy and search constraints.
- Work product: evidence ledger with claim, source, status, provenance, units, bounds, contradictions and open questions.
- Gate: a reviewer confirms coverage, source quality, conflict handling and honest unknowns.

## 2. Hypothesis and Experiment Design

Purpose: convert uncertainty into falsifiable hypotheses and discriminating tests.

- Inputs: evidence ledger, competing explanations, decision threshold and available facilities.
- Work product: experiment plan with variables, boundary conditions, controls, measurement protocol, statistical method and acceptance threshold.
- Gate: a reviewer confirms that the test can distinguish the competing hypotheses and that simulation is not presented as physical proof.

## 3. Requirements and Architecture

Purpose: convert approved evidence, mission intent and explicit assumptions into a controlled system baseline.

- Inputs: approved evidence package, stakeholder needs, constraints, interfaces and mission decisions.
- Work product: requirement set, requirement-to-evidence matrix, architecture alternatives, interfaces and open design blocks.
- Gate: every requirement traces to evidence, an assumption or an explicit mission decision; humans approve baseline promotion.

## 4. Trades, Margin and Risk

Purpose: compare alternatives without hiding uncertainty or coupling.

- Inputs: architecture set, criteria, uncertainties, failure modes, resource limits and verification burden.
- Work product: scored trade study, sensitivity analysis, margins, risk register, dissent record and recommended option.
- Gate: reviewers confirm criteria, weighting, sensitivities, dissent and risk acceptance before selection.

## 5. Verification and Validation

Purpose: prove that claims and requirements have adequate methods, results and dispositions.

- Inputs: claim set, requirement baseline, models, test assets, acceptance criteria and configuration state.
- Work product: verification cross-reference matrix with claim, source, method, result, status, discrepancy and gate state.
- Gate: independent review confirms trace completeness and closes, accepts or escalates every discrepancy.

## 6. Structured Handoff

Purpose: move work between science, engineering, verification, delivery and operations without losing meaning.

- Inputs: approved upstream package, destination contract and configuration identifiers.
- Work product: machine-readable handoff containing claims, sources, statuses, provenance, parameters, uncertainty, requirements, tests, approvals and open issues.
- Gate: the receiving stage validates schema, provenance, completeness and configuration before accepting the package.

## 7. Program Control and Release

Purpose: coordinate dependencies, decisions, gates and releases across complex physical work.

- Inputs: baselines, schedule, dependencies, risks, review calendar, approval matrix and release criteria.
- Work product: integrated plan, decision log, gate packet, configuration manifest, exception list and release recommendation.
- Gate: accountable humans approve consequential actions, risk acceptance, baseline promotion and operational release.

## 8. Mission Memory and Field Learning

Purpose: preserve what the mission knew, decided, disputed, configured and learned.

- Inputs: approved artifacts, provenance, configuration history, decisions, dissent, test results, anomalies and field observations.
- Work product: durable mission-memory record with supersession links, lessons, unresolved questions and triggers that reopen prior work.
- Gate: records pass integrity, access, retention and reconstruction checks before they become authoritative mission memory.

## Mars pilot

Start with one consequential recurring decision. Install only the skills that decision needs. Define its work products, evidence rules and gates. Reconcile the outputs against expert work. Scale only after the loop is reliable.


---

## Version 5 deployment context

The portable-skill catalog now maps to the application domains on slide 18—field science, habitat, ISRU and power, food, construction, and maintenance—and to the three principal harnesses. Each skill must declare its role, loop, tools, evidence contract, work product, ground-truth checks, memory behavior, and approval boundary so it can move between supported runtimes without losing mission discipline.
